types-of-profit-s1.title: Rosa Quill's bakery: explicit and implicit costs
types-of-profit-s1.text: Rosa Quill quit a job that paid \$45,000 a year to run her own bakery, Quill and Crumb. She also put \$50,000 of her savings into the business; in a savings account that money would have earned \$2,000 a year in interest. Last year the bakery took in \$180,000 in revenue and paid \$30,000 in rent, \$50,000 for ingredients and \$40,000 in wages to two employees. (An invented business, for practice.)

table.caption: Revenue and costs of three small firms last year, in thousands of dollars (invented data for practice)

items.q: In the scenario, what was the bakery's accounting profit last year, in dollars?

why.correct: Accounting profit = total revenue - explicit costs = $180{,}000 - (30{,}000 + 50{,}000 + 40{,}000) = 60{,}000$ dollars.

mistakes.why: That also subtracts implicit costs; that is economic profit. An accountant subtracts only the explicit costs.
That subtracts only the rent. Explicit costs also include ingredients and wages: 30,000 + 50,000 + 40,000.

items.q: In the scenario, what were Rosa's implicit costs last year, in dollars?

why.correct: Implicit costs are the income Rosa gave up: the \$45,000 salary plus the \$2,000 of interest, $45{,}000 + 2{,}000 = 47{,}000$ dollars.

mistakes.why: That counts the forgone salary but not the \$2,000 of interest her savings could have earned.
The forgone income is the \$2,000 of interest, not the \$50,000 she put in.

items.q: In the scenario, what was the bakery's economic profit last year, in dollars?

why.correct: Economic profit = revenue - explicit costs - implicit costs = $180{,}000 - 120{,}000 - 47{,}000 = 13{,}000$ dollars.

mistakes.why: That is accounting profit. Economic profit also subtracts the implicit costs of \$47,000.
That leaves out the \$2,000 of interest Rosa gave up.

items.q: In the scenario, what does the bakery's economic profit tell Rosa?
options: She would earn more by going back to her old job
The bakery just covers its explicit costs
The bakery beats her next-best choices
Her accountant has overstated the bakery's costs

why.correct: Economic profit counts every opportunity cost. A positive economic profit of \$13,000 means the bakery pays Rosa more than her best alternatives combined.
options: Her economic profit is positive, so the bakery beats the \$47,000 she gave up.
It covers its explicit costs by \$60,000, and its implicit costs too.
Right: positive economic profit means she beats the job and the savings account.
The accountant leaves out implicit costs; economic profit adds them.

items.q: Use the table. Which firm earns a normal profit?
options: Firm X
Firm Y
Firm Z
Firm Y, because its implicit costs are lowest

why.correct: Normal profit is zero economic profit: revenue just covers explicit and implicit costs. Firm X: $500 - 300 - 200 = 0$.
options: Right: 500 - 300 - 200 = 0 economic profit.
Firm Y's economic profit is 400 - 250 - 100 = 50 thousand, above normal profit.
Firm Z's economic profit is 300 - 200 - 150 = -50 thousand, below normal profit.
Low implicit costs give Firm Y a positive economic profit of 50, above normal profit.

items.q: Use the table. Which firm shows an accounting profit but has an economic loss?
options: Firm X
Firm Y
Firms X and Z
Firm Z

why.correct: Firm Z: accounting profit $300 - 200 = 100$ thousand, but its implicit costs of 150 are larger, so economic profit is $100 - 150 = -50$ thousand: an economic loss.
options: Firm X has zero economic profit, not a loss.
Firm Y earns a positive economic profit of 50 thousand.
Firm X has zero economic profit, which is not a loss.
Right: accounting profit 100, economic profit -50 thousand.

items.q: Use the table. What is Firm Y's economic profit, in thousands of dollars?

mistakes.why: That is accounting profit. Subtract the implicit costs of 100 too.
That subtracts only the implicit costs. Subtract the explicit costs of 250 as well.

items.q: Use the table. Firm Y's owner is offered a job that would raise her implicit costs from 100 to 160 thousand dollars. What would Firm Y's economic profit then be, in thousands of dollars?

why.correct: Economic profit = $400 - 250 - 160 = -10$ thousand dollars: a better outside offer raises the opportunity cost of staying, turning a profit into a loss.

mistakes.why: That is accounting profit, which does not change. Economic profit uses the new implicit costs.
Check the sign: 400 - 250 - 160 is negative. The firm would have an economic loss.

options: total revenue minus explicit and implicit costs
total revenue minus explicit costs
total revenue minus implicit costs
explicit costs minus implicit costs

why.correct: Accounting profit = total revenue - explicit costs. Economic profit also subtracts implicit costs.
options: That is economic profit.
Right: an accountant subtracts the money actually paid out.
Accounting profit subtracts explicit costs, the money paid out.
Profit starts from revenue.

items.q: Which of these is an implicit cost for a dentist who owns her own practice?
options: The rent she pays for her office
The salary she gave up at a hospital
The wages she pays her assistant
The bill for dental supplies

why.correct: An implicit cost is the value of something the owner already has (her time, her savings, her building) in its best other use; no money changes hands.
options: Rent is a payment: an explicit cost.
Right: forgone income is an opportunity cost with no payment.
Wages are paid out: an explicit cost.
A bill paid is an explicit cost.

items.q: A restaurant earns zero economic profit. Which statement is correct?
options: It has no revenue left after paying its bills
Its owner should close it at once
Its accounting profit is zero too
Its owner earns what she would elsewhere

why.correct: Zero economic profit means revenue covers every cost, including the owner's opportunity costs. The owner earns a normal profit, and no other use of her time and money pays more.
options: It has accounting profit equal to its implicit costs.
With normal profit, she does as well here as anywhere.
Accounting profit equals the implicit costs, which are above zero.
Right: zero economic profit is a normal profit.

items.q: Why is a firm's economic profit never greater than its accounting profit?
options: It subtracts implicit costs too
Economic profit uses a lower revenue figure
Accounting profit adds the owner's forgone salary
Economic profit counts fewer explicit costs

why.correct: Economic profit = accounting profit - implicit costs. Since implicit costs cannot be negative, economic profit is at most equal to accounting profit.
options: Right: subtracting more can only leave the same or less.
Both use the same total revenue.
Accounting profit leaves forgone salary out; it does not add it.
Both subtract the same explicit costs.

items.q: A landscaping firm has total revenue of \$90,000, explicit costs of \$70,000 and implicit costs of \$25,000. What is its economic profit, in dollars?

why.correct: Economic profit = $90{,}000 - 70{,}000 - 25{,}000 = -5{,}000$ dollars, an economic loss even with a \$20,000 accounting profit.

mistakes.why: That is accounting profit. Subtract the implicit costs too: 20,000 - 25,000.
Check the sign: the costs (95,000) are larger than the revenue, so the result is a loss.

items.q: Marco owns his bike shop and its building. Which of these are implicit costs of running the shop? Select all that apply.
options: The property tax he pays on the building
The salary he could earn as a mechanic at another shop
The electricity bill for the shop
The cost of bike parts he buys from a supplier

why.correct: Implicit costs are the owner's forgone income from his own resources, here the salary his time could earn elsewhere; bills and taxes he pays are explicit costs.
options: No: a tax bill is paid in money, an explicit cost.
Yes: forgone income is an implicit cost.
No: it is paid in money, an explicit cost.
No: parts are paid for, an explicit cost.

items.q: Firms in the scooter-rental business are earning large economic profits. What is likely to happen next?
options: Current owners leave to find better uses of their time
Accountants raise the firms' explicit costs
New scooter-rental firms are started
The firms' implicit costs fall to zero

why.correct: Positive economic profit means resources in this industry earn more than in their next-best use, which draws in new firms. Topic 3.6 follows what that does to price and profit.
options: They earn more here than elsewhere, so they have no reason to leave.
Explicit costs depend on payments, not on profit.
Right: economic profit signals that resources earn more here than elsewhere.
Implicit costs depend on the owners' other choices, which have not changed.

items.q: Make the explanation specific: a firm shows an accounting profit of \$30,000, and its owner gave up a \$40,000 job to run it. Fill in each blank.

why.correct: Economic profit = accounting profit - implicit costs = $30{,}000 - 40{,}000 = -10{,}000$ dollars.

specific.frame: Economic profit also subtracts ___ costs, so because the owner's ___ is larger than the accounting profit, economic profit is ___ zero.

kind.label: Which costs
options: implicit
explicit

why.1: Accounting profit already subtracts explicit costs; economic profit adds the implicit ones.

what.label: What is larger
options: forgone salary
rent payment

why.1: Rent is an explicit cost, already in accounting profit; the forgone salary is the implicit cost.

sign.label: Economic profit
options: less than
greater than

why.1: 30,000 - 40,000 = -10,000, which is less than zero: an economic loss.

specific.model: Economic profit also subtracts implicit costs, so because the owner's forgone salary of \$40,000 is larger than the \$30,000 accounting profit, economic profit is less than zero: an economic loss of \$10,000.

items.q: A firm's accounting profit is \$40,000 and its economic profit is \$10,000. What are its implicit costs, in dollars?

why.correct: Economic profit = accounting profit - implicit costs, so implicit costs = $40{,}000 - 10{,}000 = 30{,}000$ dollars.

mistakes.why: That adds the two profits. Implicit costs are the gap between them: 40,000 - 10,000.
That is the economic profit, not the implicit costs.

options: The average accounting profit of firms in the industry
Any profit above the owner's explicit costs
Zero economic profit
A loss small enough that the firm keeps going

why.correct: Normal profit is the return that just keeps the owner's resources in this business: zero economic profit.
options: Normal profit is defined by opportunity cost, not by an industry average.
That is accounting profit.
Right: the owner earns what the next-best use would pay.
Normal profit is not a loss; economic profit is exactly zero.
